text: This is Vini.
Vini has never survived anything harder than a Monday.
So when the news says the dead are walking through his city, he has one question.
Can he survive thirty days?
There's one thing you need to know before we start.
They can't see very well.
But they can hear everything.
So whatever happens...
don't make a sound.
Day one.
Vini wakes up to forty-seven missed calls, and his phone screaming an emergency alert.
Outside, someone is shouting.
Then they stop shouting.
His first instinct is to run outside and see what's going on.
That's what most people do.
And that's why most people don't make it past day one.
Rule one: on day one, stay inside.
Lock the door, close the curtains, and stay away from the windows.
In the first hours of any disaster, the streets are the most dangerous place to be.
Crashed cars, panicked crowds, and in this case... crowds that bite.
Rule two: fill everything with water.
The bath, the sink, every pan and bottle he owns.
When a city breaks down, the taps are often one of the first things to go.
A person needs at least two litres of drinking water a day, and a full bath holds well over a hundred litres.
That's weeks of water, sitting right there in the bathroom.
By midnight, the shouting outside has turned into something else.
A low groan.
Hundreds of them.
